root_cause.text: The acpi_power_meter driver’s acpi_power_meter_notify() performed hwmon_device_unregister() while holding resource->lock, even though sysfs callbacks for that hwmon device also take the same lock, creating a lock-order inversion that can deadlock during concurrent sysfs access and device reconfiguration/removal.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE/commit explicitly states that acpi_power_meter_notify() “calls hwmon_device_unregister() under a lock that is also acquired by callbacks in sysfs attributes of the device being unregistered,” and the patch fixes it by moving hwmon_device_unregister() outside resource->lock and adding a separate static mutex to serialize concurrent METER_NOTIFY_CONFIG notifications.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a dedicated ACPI notification mutex to provide synchronization and prevent concurrent access races.
intent_record.what: A new file-scope static mutex named acpi_notify_lock is introduced using DEFINE_MUTEX, added between the existing global variables and the next function definition.
intent_record.how: This makes a dedicated lock available for synchronizing code paths that handle ACPI notifications or related shared state, helping prevent concurrent access races when the lock is later used at runtime.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix ACPI power meter reconfiguration by serializing notify handling, avoiding unregister on error pointers, and releasing the resource lock before hwmon re-registration.
intent_record.what: The change adds a scoped guard for acpi_notify_lock at the start of acpi_power_meter_notify(), wraps the METER_NOTIFY_CONFIG handling with an explicit check before unregistering the hwmon device using `if (!IS_ERR(resource->hwmon_dev))`, moves `hwmon_device_unregister(resource->hwmon_dev)` to occur before `mutex_lock(&resource->lock)`, and inserts a `mutex_unlock(&resource->lock)` before calling `hwmon_device_register_with_info()`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this serializes notification handling under acpi_notify_lock, avoids calling hwmon_device_unregister() on an error-valued hwmon_dev pointer, and prevents the per-resource lock from being held across hwmon device registration. This fixes unsafe lock usage and invalid unregister behavior during configuration-change notifications, reducing the risk of deadlocks or crashes while reinitializing meter capabilities and domain devices.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove the immediate mutex unlock in the config notification path to correct lock handling around hwmon device registration.
intent_record.what: The call to mutex_unlock(&resource->lock); was removed from the code path in acpi_power_meter_notify() after attempting to register the hwmon device in the METER_NOTIFY_CONFIG case.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this prevents the mutex from being unlocked at that location, changing lock handling for the configuration notification path so the lock remains held until some other point in control flow handles it instead of releasing it immediately there.

intent_record.intent_summary: Guard hwmon device unregistration in acpi_power_meter_remove() so cleanup skips error pointers from failed registration.
intent_record.what: The code changes the unconditional call to hwmon_device_unregister(resource->hwmon_dev) in acpi_power_meter_remove() into a conditional call guarded by if (!IS_ERR(resource->hwmon_dev)).
intent_record.how: At runtime, this prevents hwmon_device_unregister() from being called with an error-encoded pointer stored in resource->hwmon_dev, avoiding invalid cleanup behavior or a potential crash during device removal when hwmon device registration previously failed.

grouping_result.intent: Add a dedicated ACPI notification mutex to provide synchronization and prevent concurrent access races.
Remove the immediate mutex unlock in the config notification path to correct lock handling around hwmon device registration.
Guard hwmon device unregistration in acpi_power_meter_remove() so cleanup skips error pointers from failed registration.

consistency_review.core_intent: Fix ACPI power meter configuration notification handling by correcting mutex/lock usage and safe hwmon device re-registration during reconfiguration.

relevance_review.reason: The root cause is unsafe synchronization in ACPI power meter notification handling leading to deadlock/races during unregister and concurrent sysfs access. Adding a dedicated ACPI notification mutex directly changes the synchronization around notifications to prevent those concurrent access issues, so it is related to the vulnerability.

The changes directly target the deadlock root cause in acpi_power_meter_notify(): they correct lock/mutex handling during configuration notifications and specifically release the resource lock before hwmon device unregister/re-registration, addressing the lock-order inversion with sysfs callbacks.

The change only adds an error-pointer guard before hwmon_device_unregister() in acpi_power_meter_remove(). It does not address the root cause deadlock from calling hwmon_device_unregister() while holding resource->lock in acpi_power_meter_notify() during concurrent sysfs access.

candidates.rationale: This is the direct deadlock trigger: it unregisters the hwmon device while resource->lock is held, and unregister can wait for sysfs callbacks that also acquire the same lock.
This lock acquisition establishes the problematic locking context that makes the subsequent hwmon_device_unregister call unsafe and able to deadlock with sysfs callbacks.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement is the direct cause of the deadlock: it unregisters the hwmon device while the code is executing under resource->lock, and hwmon/sysfs teardown can wait on callbacks that also attempt to take the same lock.

This statement establishes the locking context that makes the subsequent hwmon_device_unregister(resource->hwmon_dev); unsafe, creating the lock-order inversion with sysfs callbacks that also acquire resource->lock.

bic_trace_step.reason: The relevant logic is fully visible in `acpi_power_meter_notify()`, so the snippet is sufficient. In the `METER_NOTIFY_CONFIG` case, the code does `mutex_lock(&resource->lock);` and then, while still holding that same lock, calls `hwmon_device_unregister(resource->hwmon_dev);`. This matches the root cause exactly: unregistering the hwmon device while `resource->lock` is held. The same file also shows sysfs callbacks that take the same lock, for example `power_meter_read()` uses `guard(mutex)(&res->lock);`, `power_meter_write()` uses `guard(mutex)(&res->lock);`, and the extra attribute stores such as `power1_average_max_store()` / `power1_average_min_store()` use `mutex_lock(&res->lock);`. Since hwmon unregister can synchronize with/remove sysfs files while sysfs callbacks may be running and those callbacks also acquire `resource->lock`, this creates the lock-order inversion / deadlock scenario described. There is no fix here because `hwmon_device_unregister()` is not moved outside the locked region; instead it is explicitly executed under the lock in this commit.

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet directly shows the relevant notifier logic and the lock handling needed to assess the deadlock root cause. In `acpi_power_meter_notify()`, the old outer `mutex_lock(&resource->lock);` / `mutex_unlock(&resource->lock);` around the whole switch has been removed. Instead, only `METER_NOTIFY_CONFIG` briefly locks around `free_capabilities(resource);` and `read_capabilities(resource);`, then unlocks before attribute removal/recreation. The cases `METER_NOTIFY_TRIP`, `METER_NOTIFY_CAP`, and `METER_NOTIFY_INTERVAL` no longer call `update_meter(resource)`, `update_cap(resource)`, or `update_avg_interval(resource)` while in the notifier. This matches the fix description: the notifier no longer holds `resource->lock` while doing sysfs-related operations that can take kernfs locks. The diff also adds locking to `show_str()` with `mutex_lock(&resource->lock); ... mutex_unlock(&resource->lock);`, addressing the capability-string race mentioned in the commit message. Since the vulnerable construct was holding `resource->lock` across notifier processing and then performing sysfs attribute removal/recreation / hwmon unregister-related paths, and that broad locking is absent here, this version already contains the fix.
